questions.question: What is the purpose of the `__init__` method in a Python class?
options: It is called when the class is imported
It initializes instance attributes when a new object is created
It defines class-level attributes shared by all instances
It is the only method that can accept arguments
questions.explanation: `__init__` is the constructor—it runs automatically when you create a new instance with `MyClass()`. It sets up instance-specific attributes so each object starts with the correct initial state.

questions.question: What is the difference between class attributes and instance attributes?
options: Class attributes are defined inside `__init__`; instance attributes are defined outside
Class attributes are shared by all instances; instance attributes are unique to each object
Instance attributes use `self`; class attributes use `cls`
There is no difference—they both store the same data
questions.explanation: Class attributes are defined directly in the class body and shared by all instances (e.g., `species = 'Canis'`). Instance attributes are set via `self` in methods and are unique to each object (e.g., `self.name = name`).

questions.question: Why would you use `@property` instead of a regular attribute?
options: Properties are faster than regular attributes
Properties allow you to add validation, compute derived values, or make attributes read-only
Properties can only be used with private attributes
Properties are required for any attribute starting with an underscore
questions.explanation: `@property` lets you control attribute access with getter/setter logic without changing how callers use the attribute. Common uses: validating values on assignment, computing values from other attributes, and creating read-only attributes.

questions.question: Why must `self` be the first parameter of instance methods?
options: It is a Python keyword required for syntax
It refers to the specific instance calling the method, allowing access to instance attributes
It prevents name conflicts with global variables
It automatically initializes all attributes
questions.explanation: `self` is a reference to the instance on which the method was called. Python passes it automatically—`obj.method()` is equivalent to `MyClass.method(obj)`. Without `self`, instance methods cannot access or modify instance attributes.

questions.question: What does `__str__` define for a class?
options: The string used as the class name
The human-readable string representation returned by `print()` and `str()`
The internal memory address of the object
The list of all attributes on the object
questions.explanation: `__str__` is the dunder method that controls what `print(obj)` and `str(obj)` display. It should return a human-readable description. `__repr__` is for developer/debug strings. If `__str__` is not defined, Python falls back to `__repr__`.
